rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their plea that they seek the Almighty’s forgiveness meets a people who persist in polytheism and disobedience; verse 20 further explains their response.
rows.anchor: calls of seeking forgiveness from the Almighty, his people have become adamant on their polytheism and disobedience. Verse 20 further explains this.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Istikbār means deliberately opposing truth and rebelling against it.
rows.anchor: deliberately oppose the truth and to display rebelliousness before it. Whether small or big, truths are dear to God.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even difficult truths are dear to God and must be accepted; rejecting truth follows Satan’s practice and makes the rejecter his accomplice.
rows.anchor: Whether small or big, truths are dear to God. For this reason, it is essential that a person submits to them

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance is the real cause of plugging their ears, covering themselves, and persisting in polytheism.
rows.anchor: is mentioned as the real reason for their attitude. In other words, it was because of

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah’s shift in verse 8 marks the third phase of his mission: he intensifies his preaching when people resist.
rows.anchor: In these very eloquent words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets increase their effort and fervor as people become more averse; opposition magnifies truth’s majesty and energizes its advocates.
rows.anchor: A look at the preaching missions of the prophets of God shows that this has remained a common feature of their mission.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah used both forceful public calls and intimate private appeals whenever each approach fit the opportunity.
rows.anchor: where it was needed that the message be presented in the open in a forceful manner, Noah (sws) did so without any hesitation

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He exhausted every opportunity to awaken those still able to accept, giving them time to consider their fate before the decisive moment.
rows.anchor: The objective was to stir those who still had some ability left in them to accept the truth

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verbal noun is elided after Noah’s appeal that he openly called them, as it is after the cited verb.
rows.anchor: A verbal noun is suppressed after

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere turning to God suffices for forgiveness; alleged deities need not intercede, since God is most forgiving and merciful to repentant people.
rows.anchor: in order to earn forgiveness from Him, merely turning to Him is enough; the intercession of their alleged deities is not at all required.

rows.speaker: polytheists
rows.claim: Polytheists imagine God too exalted and remote for direct prayer, so they seek intercessors; Islahi links this notion to 39:3 and says the Qur’an refutes it.
rows.anchor: the polytheists of every period have remained in the misconception that since so exalted is the Almighty

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-samāʾ in the promise of abundant rain refers to clouds.
rows.anchor: refers to clouds, as has been explained earlier in this exegesis.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Midrāran describes rain-bearing clouds producing much rain; the word is used in both masculine and feminine forms.
rows.anchor: means clouds which produce a lot of rain. It is used equally in the masculine and feminine gender.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance will draw God’s mercy, bringing abundant rain, wealth, offspring, and other resources of life.
rows.anchor: their repentance will stir the mercy of the Almighty and He will bless them with a lot of wealth and offspring and abundant resources of life.

rows.speaker: polytheists
rows.claim: Polytheists credited deities with rain and children, feared criticizing them would cost these favors, opposed messengers for degrading them, and blamed them for trials.
rows.anchor: The polytheists were under the false notion that it was their deities who would send down rain

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah refutes that superstition: God, not the deities, controls provisions and rain, and repentance elicits mercy; the theme also appears in Hūd 11:52.
rows.anchor: Noah (sws) has rebutted this false notion of theirs. He has informed them that it is not their deities who are in charge

rows.speaker: ‘Umar
rows.claim: Reports attribute to ʿUmar that while leading the rain prayer he sought God’s forgiveness without asking for rain, explaining that repentance opens God’s mercy and He knows people’s needs.
rows.anchor: It is actually attributed to ‘Umar (rta). It is mentioned in various narratives that once while

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Verse 12 elaborates the prior promise: God grants wealth, children, orchards, and canals, not the deities; repentance pleases Him.
rows.anchor: This is just a further elaboration of what is discussed

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating the verb yajʿal emphasizes the great value and appeal of these favors.
rows.anchor: has emphasized the great value and attraction of these favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah expresses amazement at his people’s foolishness and asks why they evade his loving call to seek forgiveness.
rows.anchor: These words of Noah (sws) express amazement at the foolishness of his people.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah challenges their assumption that they can persist in evil without God’s anger appearing, despite receiving all their favors from Him.
rows.anchor: do they think that they will remain engrossed in their evil practices and the anger of God

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sūrah al-Infitār 82:6 raises the same question of what has diverted people from their gracious Lord.
rows.anchor: discusses this subject in the following words

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving abundant favors while facing no immediate seizure can make people stubborn and indifferent to accountability, though the favors require gratitude and answerability.
rows.anchor: when man receives abundant favours from God and also observes that he can do whatever he wants to and still God does not seize him

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s generosity is meant to elicit gratitude and awareness of future accountability; no one can escape His grasp then.
rows.anchor: it is a requisite of these favours that he remain grateful to God and also realize that one day he will be held accountable for these favours

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tarjawna means to expect or hope.
rows.anchor: here means “to expect and to hope”

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waqāran means glory, grandeur, and fury.
rows.anchor: means “glory, grandeur and fury.” Besides the attributes of grandeur, the Almighty also has attributes of fury

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s attributes include wrath toward those who disobey and reject messengers; staying balanced requires awareness of both majesty and fury, and this sūrah emphasizes wrath because it addresses the arrogant.
rows.anchor: Besides the attributes of grandeur, the Almighty also has attributes of fury which manifest themselves on people who disobey and reject His Messengers.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phases of human creation show that the Creator can readily recreate people after death and dust; the resurrection will expose and punish the criminals and arrogant.
rows.anchor: if a person reflects merely on all the phases of his creation, he can easily understand that the Almighty Who has shown such creativity can have no difficulty in re-creating man

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an uses the same creation-based proof for resurrection in al-Ḥajj 22:5–6 and also discusses it in al-Mu’minūn 23:14–16.
rows.anchor: This argument with precisely the same context has been expressed at various other places in the Qur’ān in order to substantiate the Day of Judgement.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the six verses could be read as part of Noah’s speech, Islahi prefers to see them as divine insertions; verse 21’s renewed ‘Noah said, My Lord’ marks the transition back to his prayer.
rows.anchor: it seems to me that these are insertions from the Almighty in order to complete Noah’s speech.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven heavens are the universe’s most prominent sign: their Creator can recreate human beings after death.
rows.anchor: the Almighty has directed man’s attention to the most prominent sign of His universe: the seven heavens.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same creation argument appears in al-Nāziʿāt 79:27 and, in a different style, al-Maʿārij 70:40–41.
rows.anchor: Precisely this same argument is found in the following verse of Sūrah al-Nāzi‘āt

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭibāq means layered, one above another; it need not mean seven successive folds of one sky, but seven elevated distinct worlds, each with seven heavens.
rows.anchor: means “multi-layered; one above the other.” This does not necessarily mean that, like the folds of a cloth, the sky has seven consecutive folds

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qur’anic descriptions of the heavens display God’s infinite power; it is enough to accept them broadly, since only God can unveil their reality on the Day of Judgment.
rows.anchor: It is enough to believe in them in the broad sense. The reality will manifest on the Day the Almighty will unveil it.
